newsitem.title: INDIA: India state radio launches Internet service.
newsitem.headline: India state radio launches Internet service.

text.p: The state-run All India Radio launched a real-time broadcast service on the Internet on Monday, the broadcaster said in a statement.
"With the flick of a button, the selected programme will start playing in real-time on the speakers attached to the computer," the statement said.

Along with news updates in Hindi and English, the service (http://air.kode.net) would also broadcast current affairs, music, drama, speeches, discussions and items from the radio's archives, it added.
State-run All India Radio has a monopoly over radio broadcasting in the country, but rents out time slots in frequency modulation (FM) stations to private broadcasters.
It has a network of 172 full-fledged stations across India.
